questions.question: What does rememberSaveable give you beyond remember?
options: The value is shared across all composables with the same name
The value is kept even after the user swipes the app away from Recents
The value is written to DataStore after every change
The value also survives config changes and process death
questions.explanation: rememberSaveable registers its value with the SaveableStateRegistry, which writes it into the saved instance Bundle. That covers rotation and system-initiated process death, but not the user dismissing the task, which drops saved state. It's not persistent storage.

questions.question: Setting `savedStateHandle["query"] = value` immediately writes the value to disk.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: SavedStateHandle keeps values in memory and hands them over when the owner saves its state (onSaveInstanceState), as part of the Bundle the system keeps. Nothing is written to app storage, which is also why the data is lost if the user clears the task.

questions.question: You want to keep a plain (non-Parcelable) data class in rememberSaveable. What is the usual approach?
options: Mark the class @Stable so the registry can save it
Wrap the value in mutableStateOf before passing it in
Provide a Saver (e.g. mapSaver) that converts it to Bundle-friendly values
Store it with plain remember and add a key so the runtime can restore it
questions.explanation: The saved Bundle can only hold types a Bundle supports, such as primitives, Strings, Parcelables and Serializables. A Saver converts the object to and from such values; @Parcelize is the other common option. @Stable is a compiler hint and doesn't make anything saveable.

questions.question: Which is the right way to expose a search query that survives process death as a Flow from a ViewModel?
options: `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow("query", "")`, written via `savedStateHandle["query"] = q`
`val query = MutableStateFlow(savedStateHandle["query"] ?: "")`, updated via `query.value = q`
`val query = flowOf(savedStateHandle.get<String>("query"))`, updated by recreating the flow
`val query = savedStateHandle.getLiveData<String>("query").value`, updated via postValue
questions.explanation: getStateFlow returns a StateFlow backed by the handle, so writing through the handle both emits and persists. A MutableStateFlow seeded from the handle reads the restored value once, but later updates never reach saved state, so they are lost on process death.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be put into saved instance state? Select all that apply.
options: A few hundred items of data loaded from the network
Text the user has typed into a form but not submitted
A Bitmap of the user's profile picture
The index of the currently selected tab
An object that holds a reference to a Context
questions.explanation: Saved state should be small and describe the UI: user input, selections, IDs. Loaded data and bitmaps risk hitting the Binder size limit and can be refetched. Contexts can't be meaningfully saved and would leak or fail. Typed text and tab index are exactly what it is for.

questions.question: An item in a LazyColumn (with stable keys) holds one value in remember and another in rememberSaveable. The item scrolls off screen and back. What happens?
options: Both values are lost, since the item left the composition
Both values are kept, since lazy items are never disposed
The saveable value is restored; the remember one starts over
The remember value is kept; the rememberSaveable one is cleared
questions.explanation: Lazy layouts dispose items that scroll out, so remember is lost. But they wrap each item in a SaveableStateHolder keyed by the item key, so saveable state is stored when the item leaves and given back when it returns. That's also why keys should be stable and Bundle-friendly.

questions.question: By default, rememberSaveable saves its value under a key derived from its position in the composition, so restructuring the composable tree between save and restore can stop it from being restored.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Without an explicit key, rememberSaveable uses the composite key hash of where it's called. If the tree around it differs when state is restored, the hash differs and the value isn't found. Passing an explicit key avoids that.

questions.question: A component calls `savedStateRegistry.consumeRestoredStateForKey("pager")` and gets a Bundle. What does a second call with the same key return?
options: The same Bundle again, as restored state is immutable
An empty Bundle, since the registry never returns null for a registered key
null, as restored state is released once it is consumed
It throws IllegalStateException for consuming a key twice
questions.explanation: consumeRestoredStateForKey hands over the restored Bundle once and then drops its reference, so a second call returns null. Components should read restored state once at setup and register a SavedStateProvider to provide fresh state on the next save.

questions.question: Which statements about SaveableStateHolder are true? Select all that apply.
options: Navigation Compose uses it so a destination's rememberSaveable state survives while it is on the back stack
It keeps ViewModels alive for content that is not currently composed
SaveableStateProvider(key) restores the saved state for that key when content re-enters composition
removeState(key) discards the saved state for a key that will not come back
questions.explanation: SaveableStateHolder stores the rememberSaveable state of content that leaves composition, keyed by an id, and restores it when content with the same key comes back; removeState drops it. ViewModels are not involved: their lifetime comes from the ViewModelStoreOwner, such as the back stack entry.

questions.question: Where does a ViewModel's SavedStateHandle get its initial values?
options: From the owner's restored saved state plus default args (e.g. nav arguments)
From the ViewModel's constructor default parameter values, captured by the factory
From DataStore, read synchronously at ViewModel creation
From the previous ViewModel instance's fields after rotation
questions.explanation: The handle is built from the owner's SavedStateRegistry (state restored after recreation or process death) merged with default args, which is how navigation arguments appear in it. It is unrelated to DataStore, and it isn't copied from old ViewModel fields.
